tools.name: range_position
tools.description: Where one reading of one LOINC sits against its Anchor v3 published range: below, within or above it, bounds inclusive. pick latest takes the newest reading in the window, pick at the reading at `at`. A sex- or age-specific range is chosen from the subject's stored sex and birth year; facts_used names them, and the age is approximate (birth year only: one of two ages). When a fact is not stored (timing never is) or the age band changes within the reading's year, position is null and depends_on names the facts; nothing is guessed. Reads up to 5000 rows; refuses no rows, mixed units, no published range, and a unit other than the range's (nothing is converted). Neutral position only.

tools.name: convert_unit
tools.description: Convert one value of glucose, creatinine, HbA1c, total/LDL/HDL cholesterol, triglycerides or body temperature between units with a fixed table: value rounded half away from zero, unrounded, unit, the formula used and the rounding rule. Reads no rows. A pair the table does not hold is refused with UNSUPPORTED_CONVERSION and the pairs it does hold.

inputSchema.description: One value of one analyte from one unit to another, by a fixed table

tools.name: cohort_position
tools.description: Where a subject's latest value of one LOINC in a time range sits among the latest values, in the same window, of everyone in its synthetic cohort (one value per person, the subject included). percentile is the mid-rank percentile, 100 × (n_lower + n_equal / 2) / n, where n is the people with a value and n_equal counts the subject; say it as "higher than about <percentile> % of the <n> synthetic people with a value", never better, worse or normal. Synthetic cohorts only. Refuses no value for the subject, fewer than 10 people with a value, mixed units across the cohort, and more than 20000 cohort rows (narrow the window).

tools.name: conditions_timeline

tools.name: sleep_summary
tools.description: Main sleep per night in a window, one row per source and night: duration (min), time in bed (min, Whoop), efficiency (%) and the source's own sleep score, with each source's averages. Oura's main sleep is its long_sleep period; Whoop naps are left out. A field a source does not record is null. Personal mode: this turn's linked wearables, no subject_ref. tools.name: cross_source_compare
tools.description: How closely two linked wearables agree on one daily measure (hrv, resting_hr, sleep_duration, sleep_efficiency) in a window, over the days both recorded: n_pairs, each source's mean, the mean difference (b minus a), its standard deviation, the limits of agreement (mean difference plus or minus 1.96 standard deviations) and the Pearson correlation. Under 7 paired days the spread, limits and correlation are null. Personal mode only; units must match and are never converted. Says how far apart the two read, never which is right. Refuses SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED, NO_ROWS, MIXED_UNITS, UNIT_MISMATCH and WINDOW_TOO_SHORT.
